text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"WAL mode first appeared in SQLite 3.7.0.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage states that the WAL option became available beginning with version 3.7.0.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new \"Write-Ahead Log\" option (hereafter referred to as \"WAL\") is available."}]},{"claim_text":"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL is persistent.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage explicitly says that journal_mode=WAL is persistent, unlike other journaling modes.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"Unlike the other journaling modes, PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL is persistent."}]},{"claim_text":"Simply closing and reopening a WAL database is not enough to change its page size.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passages say page_size cannot be changed after entering WAL mode and that closing and reopening a WAL database leaves it in WAL mode.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL mode"},{"index":2,"quote":"If a process sets WAL mode, then closes and reopens the database, the database will come back in WAL mode."}]},{"claim_text":"You have to switch back to a rollback journal mode first to change a WAL database's page size.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage states that a rollback journal mode is required to change the page size.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"You must be in a rollback journal mode to change the page size."}]},{"claim_text":"From version 3.7.0 until 3.22.0, reading a WAL-mode database required write access.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"WAL became available in 3.7.0, and the passage says older versions required write access to read a WAL-mode database, with that constraint relaxed beginning in 3.22.0.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"Older versions of SQLite could not read a WAL-mode database that was read-only. In other words, write access was required in order to read a WAL-mode database. This constraint was relaxed beginning with SQLite version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22)."},{"index":4,"quote":"Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new \"Write-Ahead Log\" option (hereafter referred to as \"WAL\") is available."}]},{"claim_text":"SQLite's default page size is 4096 bytes.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passages do not state SQLite's default page size.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"Converting a database to WAL fails if the VFS does not support the necessary shared-memory primitives.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage gives lack of VFS support for shared-memory primitives as an example of when conversion to WAL could not be completed.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"If the conversion to WAL could not be completed (for example, if the VFS does not support the necessary shared-memory primitives) then the journaling mode will be unchanged and the string returned from the primitive will be the prior journaling mode (for example \"delete\")."}]},{"claim_text":"In that case, the journal_mode pragma returns an error.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passage says the pragma returns a string and that on failed conversion it returns the prior journaling mode, not an error.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"The journal_mode pragma returns a string which is the new journal mode. On success, the pragma will return the string \"wal\". If the conversion to WAL could not be completed (for example, if the VFS does not support the necessary shared-memory primitives) then the journaling mode will be unchanged and the string returned from the primitive will be the prior journaling mode (for example \"delete\")."}]}]}
